summary: Master UDL Guidelines 3.0, MTSS, and differentiated instruction in this 5-day inclusive education training. Enroll to design barrier-free curricula today.
lede: Inclusive education and universal design for learning help education professionals identify barriers and plan for learner variability. Designed for practitioners in formal and non-formal learning settings, the course develops practical skills in reviewing curriculum barriers, applying UDL checkpoints to lesson design, and creating differentiated assessments and tiered supports. It also covers evaluating digital learning materials for accessibility and assistive technology compatibility.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for education professionals at intermediate level who already work within formal or non-formal learning environments and are ready to move beyond awareness of inclusion principles into applied curriculum redesign and systemic implementation.
modules: Barrier Analysis and Learner Variability Profiling
Multi-Tiered Systems of Support (MTSS) and Intervention Planning
Accessible Digital Learning and Assistive Technology
prerequisites: Participants should bring a sample lesson plan, unit outline, or training module from their own professional context to use in applied workshop exercises throughout the course. A laptop or tablet is required for digital accessibility audit activities. All course materials, UDL planning templates, the CAST Guidelines 3.0 Graphic Organizer, the MTSS intervention planning template, the WCAG 2.2 audit checklist, and the differentiated assessment design framework will be provided in digital format. No specialist software licences are required; all tools used in the course are freely available or browser-based.
